title: Contract Pricing Agreement Substitute Claims: Invoice Settlement Multiplier
content:
## Invoice settlement multiplier — Contract Pricing Agreement substitute claims

A price claim on a protected substitute's shipment under a Contract Pricing Agreement carries a settlement multiplier set by how the claimed invoice was billed and paid on the customer's Commercial Credit Account. The invoice's tax rate is its sales tax over its merchandise subtotal; its discount rate is the prompt-payment cash discount earned on it over its merchandise subtotal.

| Invoice | Settlement multiplier |
|---|---|
| Carried sales tax and earned a discount | One plus the tax rate less the discount rate (the discount was earned on the merchandise only, never on the sales tax) |
| Carried sales tax without a discount | One plus the tax rate |
| Earned a discount without sales tax | One less the discount rate |
| Any other invoice | 1 |

The multiplier multiplies the unrounded claim amount — the overbilling per unit multiplied by the claim quantity — before the claim amount's rounding to the cent.

Hypothetical example: merchandise subtotal 1000.00, sales tax 70.00, cash discount earned 20.00: tax rate 0.07, discount rate 0.02, multiplier 1.05; an unrounded claim amount of 100.00 becomes 105.00.
